expectations.text: The response distinguishes a backoffice Health Check from a health probe endpoint
expectations.evidence: Neither final.md nor transcript.md mentions health probe endpoints, orchestrators, load balancers, or any distinction between the backoffice 'Health Check' dashboard and .NET health probe endpoints. The response only discusses the Settings > Health Check dashboard; there is no acknowledgement that a separate 'health probe' concept exists.

expectations.text: The implementation uses a stable HealthCheck attribute with a unique GUID, concise name, description, and Security group
expectations.evidence: final.md lines 12-16: `[HealthCheck("7E8F0B1A-4D0D-4C12-9AA1-3B6DA1E56D2F", "Production HTTPS setting", Description = "Verifies that Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps is enabled in production.", Group = "Security")]` — includes a unique GUID, a concise name, a description, and Group = "Security".

expectations.text: The check reads Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps and treats true as the recommended accepted value
expectations.evidence: final.md line 19: `private const string SettingPath = "Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps";` and line 48: `var enabled = _configuration.GetValue<bool?>(SettingPath) == true;` with a Success result only when enabled is true, matching the recommended/accepted value of true.

expectations.text: The response links to the official .md Health Check documentation and gives Settings > Health Check verification steps
expectations.evidence: The documentation link used is `https://docs.umbraco.com/umbraco-cms/run-in-production/infrastructure-and-ops/health-check` (final.md line 21), which omits the `.md` suffix that the official docs site uses for its Markdown-served Health Check page (confirmed live: the page itself advertises the `.md` variant at `.../health-check.md`, and the project's own umbraco-health-check SKILL.md explicitly links to `.../health-check.md`). The Settings > Health Check verification steps themselves are present and detailed (final.md lines 82-91), but the specific '.md' documentation link requirement is not met.

expectations.text: If a buildable project exists, the agent reports a successful build only after running it; otherwise it explicitly says build verification was unavailable
expectations.evidence: transcript.md: 'No build or tests were run because no repository implementation was made; the final answer states this honestly.' final.md line 92: 'This is a code-only answer; no project files were modified and no build or test was run.' The agent explicitly discloses that no build verification occurred rather than falsely claiming success.

suggestions.assertion: The response links to the official .md Health Check documentation and gives Settings > Health Check verification steps
suggestions.reason: This bundles two distinct checks (a specific '.md' URL suffix, and verification steps) into one pass/fail. The run satisfies the verification-steps half thoroughly but fails only on the URL suffix technicality, which may be stricter than most reviewers would consider 'linking to the official documentation' (the page it links to IS the official Health Check doc, just without the .md extension). Consider splitting this into two separate expectations so partial compliance is visible.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are reasonably well-targeted and none look trivially satisfiable by a wrong answer. The health-probe-vs-health-check distinction is a genuinely useful check this run fails outright. The '.md link' wording is oddly specific for expectation text but is verifiable against the project's own skill docs, so it's a fair (if narrow) check.
